title: Token Budget Fusion — probe notebook
content:
Goal:
- Sketch a compact API + runtime-side fusion semantics for 'token budget' hints coming from clients, SDKs, edge proxies.
- Make it work with batching/prefetching and with runtime cost-estimates (per-model per-configuration).
- Keep the shape small so product teams can experiment without deep integration.

Motivation / problem statement:
- Clients (mobile/web) want to limit spend or tail-latency by providing a soft 'token budget' per logical interaction (e.g., 200 tokens max).
- Runtime has better telemetry and can convert budget -> SLOs (max latency) or cost constraints, but client hints are useful for allocation and prefetch aggressiveness.
- When requests are batched or prefetched, multiple client budgets must be reconciled (fused). Need deterministic, auditable, and simple rule set.

High-level design ideas:
1) Client sends an optional BudgetHint in request header/body.
2) Ingress merges BudgetHints for batched requests into a BatchBudget (fused).
3) Serving runtime uses BatchBudget + model cost estimates to decide (a) whether to prefetch/kv-warm, (b) whether to truncate response, (c) whether to route to cheaper model variant.
4) Runtime returns an enforcement / accounting summary in response metadata.

Primary constraints:
- Backwards compatible: missing BudgetHint => default behavior.
- Non-binding: client hint should not be able to silently force an unsafe truncation without visible signal.
- Deterministic fusion: same set of hints => same BatchBudget independent of order.

API shape (proposal):
- BudgetHint (client) fields: all optional
  - budget_tokens: integer (soft max tokens for model output)
  - priority: string enum {low, normal, high}  (affects admission/batching)
  - cost_sensitivity: float [0.0..1.0] (0 prefer low cost, 1 prefer quality)
  - max_latency_ms: integer (soft SLO; runtime may prefer this over tokens)
  - ttl_seconds: integer (how long hint remains valid for prefetch reuse)
  - reason: short string (freeform, e.g., "quick-reply", "user-initiated-summary")

- BatchBudget (fused) fields: produced by ingress; read-only for clients
  - fused_max_tokens: integer (deterministic merge result)
  - fused_priority: string (resolved priority)
  - fused_cost_sensitivity: float
  - effective_max_latency_ms: integer
  - fused_sources: list[string] (ids of requests contributing)
  - fusion_strategy: string enum {min, median, weighted_mean, latency-first}

Fusion rules (first-pass):
- If any request has priority==high -> fused_priority=high. Else normal->normal unless all low->low.
- fused_max_tokens = min(non-null budget_tokens) if fusion_strategy==min (safe default).
- if fusion_strategy==weighted_mean -> weighted by request size (client-provided context_tokens) or 1 if absent.
- fused_cost_sensitivity = max(cost_sensitivity) (prefer higher sensitivity to avoid cost bleed).
- effective_max_latency_ms = min(non-null max_latency_ms) unless there is contradiction -> pick lower (conservative).

Rationale: conservative defaults avoid unexpectedly overspending batched budget.

Ingress pseudocode (sketch):
- inputs: array of requests R
- hints = [r.budget_hint for r in R if present]
- if empty -> BatchBudget = null (no fusion)
- else compute fused fields per strategy
- annotate batch header: x-batch-budget: Base64(JSON(BatchBudget)) or structured proto in internal path

Runtime decision points using BatchBudget:
- Model variant selection: if fused_cost_sensitivity > 0.7 and cheaper variant is within delta quality -> route to cheaper quantized variant.
- Prefetch intensity: ttl_seconds and fused_max_tokens: longer TTL + small fused_max_tokens -> reuse/merge prefetched prefixes conservatively.
- Truncation policy: only truncate if fused_max_tokens < model_min_response_tokens OR client explicitly allows truncation (flag allow_truncate:true) -> else prefer routing fallback.

Response metadata (what we return):
- x-budget-enforcement: Base64(JSON({"final_token_cap": 180, "enforced": "soft"|"hard", "chosen_variant": "mistral-7b-q4", "notes": "fused min of 180/200/300"}))
- This helps client UI show estimated truncation and billing signal.

Example request (sketch):
POST /v1/generate\Headers: Authorization, Content-Type: application/json\Body:
{
  "input": "Summarize article...",
  "budget_hint": {
    "budget_tokens": 200,
    "priority": "normal",
    "cost_sensitivity": 0.2,
    "ttl_seconds": 30,
    "reason": "preview-card"
  }
}

When batched with another request having budget_tokens:300 and priority:low, fusion_strategy=min -> fused_max_tokens=200 -> both responses may be truncated to 200 tokens by runtime unless allow_truncate is false.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Should fusion be min-by-default? It errs on safety but hurts high-budget requests co-batched with low-budget ones. Could add opt-in 'isolate' flag from clients (request_isolation:true) that prevents fusion for that request at the cost of batching efficiency.
- Auditing: need to persist fused_batch map to tie billing and debug. Adds storage overhead.
- Security: clients can set insane budgets to try to force higher resource allocation; we must gate budgets per-tenant cap with admission control.
- UX: should SDKs surface the enforced cap quickly? Possibly via streaming response metadata.

Experiment plan / rollout notes:
- Phase 0: surface BudgetHint in SDKs as opt-in; runtime collects telemetry (no enforcement).
- Phase 1: enable fusion in ingress, runtime logs decision but returns enforcement=enforced:"none" to clients. Measure tail-latency, token-cost delta.
- Phase 2: soft enforcement for low-risk customers / low percent of traffic. Add allow_truncate flag opt-in.
- Phase 3: full enforcement with tenant caps and isolation rules; expose dashboard metrics in Console (per-route token cap collisions).

Telemetry to capture (minimum):
- per-request: client_budget_tokens, client_cost_sensitivity, final_token_cap, enforced, chosen_variant, batch_size, prefetch_reused boolean
- per-batch: fusion_strategy, fused_fields, contributing_request_ids
- anomalies: number of requests where fused_max_tokens < request.budget_tokens

Implementation notes / integration points:
- Ingress: add BudgetHint parser, deterministic fusion module (idempotent). Store fused_sources as short ids (trace id).
- SRE: consider rate limit on batch size for fused budgets to keep batch fusion compute O(n) manageable.
- Billing: need mapping from fused decision to token accounting—prefer per-request actual tokens produced, but tag with fused batch id for RCA.

Quick ASCII diagram (very high level):
CLIENTS -> INGRESS (parse hints, fuse -> BatchBudget) -> ROUTER -> SERVING NODE (model variants + prefetch + enforcement) -> RESPONSE (x-budget-enforcement header) -> CLIENT

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add CLI tool to simulate batches from synthetic clients with varying budgets.
- Draft GH PR for proto schema and keep it small: BudgetHint + BatchBudget proto. (see linked PR placeholder).
- Check with billing team: can fused behavior cause unexpected invoice spikes? Schedule chat.
- Add an 'isolation' opt-in flag and measure drop in batching efficiency before proposing product change.
- Write a small bench to compare latency/cost when fusion_strategy==min vs weighted_mean for typical mobile parity traffic.

Small prototype proto (text):
syntax = "proto3";
message BudgetHint {
  int32 budget_tokens = 1;
  string priority = 2;
  double cost_sensitivity = 3;
  int32 max_latency_ms = 4;
  int32 ttl_seconds = 5;
  string reason = 6;
  bool allow_truncate = 7;
}
message BatchBudget {
  int32 fused_max_tokens = 1;
  string fused_priority = 2;
  double fused_cost_sensitivity = 3;
  int32 effective_max_latency_ms = 4;
  repeated string fused_sources = 5;
  string fusion_strategy = 6;
}

Endnotes:
- Keep this notebook intentionally informal. Want to iterate quickly; goal is to land a small proto + ingress fusion with opt-in SDK flag for next quarter.
- Related: INF-4921 (batch budgeting audit), runtime PR #1187 (proto stub).
